title: Cheapest Way to Host a Blog in India in 2026 (Real Rupee Breakdown)
html:
You do not need to spend ₹12,000 every year on GoDaddy or fall for deceptive introductory hosting discounts to run a professional, monetized blog in India. By shifting from an outdated shared cPanel server to a static Next.js build on Cloudflare's global edge network, I reduced my total annual blogging expenses to just ₹850 per year—the cost of the domain name itself. Here is the exact rupee breakdown, the 18% GST traps to watch out for, and how to set up lightning-fast blog hosting for under ₹75 per month.

Last updated: 13 Nov 2026. All domain registration fees, cloud hosting prices, and GST calculations cited below are verified against active Indian registrar and cloud provider checkout screens as of November 2026.

The Hidden Financial Traps of Indian Shared Hosting

Most Indian tech bloggers start with shared hosting because affiliates flood YouTube with promises of "hosting for ₹79/month". When I started TrendsWheel, I fell into the exact same trap. Here are the three hidden costs that hit Indian creators when the bills actually come due:

  1. The 18% GST Shock at Checkout: Indian hosting companies always display pre-tax prices on their marketing banners. When you reach the payment gateway with UPI or NetBanking, an extra 18% Goods and Services Tax (GST) is tacked on. A plan advertised at ₹10,188 jumps to ₹12,021.84 at checkout, as shown in my GoDaddy renewal invoice.
  2. The 300% Renewal Multiplier: Introductory rates are loss leaders. A shared host will happily charge you ₹149/month for your first year. But once your articles are indexed and you depend on their server, the renewal price jumps to ₹349–₹699/month plus GST. If you don't pay, your site is taken offline.
  3. Forex and Card Markups on International Cloud Hosts: If you try to escape cPanel by using foreign cloud providers like DigitalOcean ($6/mo) or Vercel Pro ($20/mo), your Indian bank will charge a 3.5% foreign currency transaction fee plus 18% GST on that fee. A $20/month bill quietly turns into nearly ₹1,850 every single month.

The Real Cost Comparison: 4 Ways to Host in India (2026)

Here is what it genuinely costs to host an active 150-post blog in India across a 3-year period:

Hosting Architecture Year 1 Cost (incl. GST) Year 2 Renewal 3-Year Total Cost Performance in India
1. GoDaddy Web Hosting Deluxe ~₹5,500 (Promo) ₹12,021.84 ₹29,543.68 Sluggish TTFB (~600ms–1200ms)
2. Hostinger Business Shared ₹3,526 (48-mo lock-in) ₹7,065 / yr ₹17,656.00 Moderate (Mumbai data center)
3. Managed Cloud VPS (Hetzner + DO) ₹7,800 / yr ₹7,800 / yr ₹23,400.00 Fast, but heavy sysadmin time
4. Static Next.js on Cloudflare Pages ₹0 ₹0 ₹0.00 Blazing fast (<50ms edge TTFB)

The ₹75/Month Setup: How TrendsWheel Actually Runs

To eliminate hosting costs permanently without sacrificing ad revenue or speed, I split my blog into two clean components:

  1. The Domain Name (The Only Paid Expense): Buy your domain from a transparent registrar (like Spaceship, Dynadot, or Cloudflare Registrar) where renewals are flat and fair. A .in domain costs around ₹550–₹750/year, while a .com costs approximately ₹850–₹950/year.
  2. The Hosting & CDN (100% Free): Upload a pre-rendered static export of your site (built with Next.js or Astro) directly to Cloudflare Pages. Cloudflare caches your HTML and images across edge servers in Mumbai, Delhi, Chennai, Bangalore, and Hyderabad.

Your total monthly cost: ₹850 / 12 = ₹70.83 per month. You pay zero rupees for hosting, zero rupees for SSL certificates, and zero rupees for bandwidth.

Step-by-Step: Rebuilding Your Blog on the Zero-Cost Stack

If you currently have a WordPress or Laravel blog on expensive shared hosting, here is how you move to the ₹75/month stack:

Step 1: Choose Next.js Static Export or Astro

Configure your static site generator to compile pure HTML at build time. In Next.js, add one line to your config:

// next.config.mjs
const nextConfig = {
  output: 'export',
  images: { unoptimized: true },
};
export default nextConfig;

When you run npm run build, the compiler turns all your Markdown or JSON articles into standalone .html files inside an out/ directory.

Step 2: Deploy to Cloudflare Pages via Wrangler CLI

Install Cloudflare's free deployment tool and upload your built directory in under 30 seconds:

npx wrangler deploy out --name yourblog --compatibility-date 2026-10-23

Cloudflare automatically assigns a free global preview domain and provisions SSL.

Step 3: Point Your Domain Nameservers

In your domain registrar dashboard (whether it's GoDaddy, Namecheap, or Google Domains), change your nameservers to Cloudflare's assigned nameservers. Once saved, Cloudflare acts as your authoritative DNS, Web Application Firewall (WAF), and global CDN without charging a single rupee.

What About Google AdSense in India?

A common misconception among Indian bloggers is that static sites cannot run advertisements. That is completely false.

Google AdSense is purely a client-side JavaScript tag. When a visitor's browser loads your static HTML, Google's adsbygoogle.js script fetches relevant ads in real time. Because static pages load in under 300 milliseconds on Indian 4G/5G mobile connections, ad viewability scores increase, which actually improves your Average RPM (Revenue Per Mille).

Just remember to place your authorized ads.txt file in your public/ folder so Google can verify your ad inventory immediately.

Who Should (and Shouldn't) Use This Setup

  • This setup is ideal for: Independent bloggers, tech reviewers, affiliate marketers, tutorials sites, and portfolio owners in India who want to keep 100% of their earnings without feeding hosting companies.
  • Do NOT use this setup if: You run an online shopping store with WooCommerce dynamic carts, a membership forum with user logins, or if you refuse to learn basic command-line commands.

The Verdict

Blogging in India should not be an expensive hobby. Spending ₹12,021 on shared hosting renewals when you can achieve 10x faster load times on Cloudflare Pages for ₹0 is financial waste.

Keep your domain registration active, ditch dynamic cPanel hosting, and run your blog on modern static edge architecture. To see how we moved our 150-post blog, read our flagship migration story, our cPanel migration checklist, and our hands-on benchmark of free hosting options.

Frequently Asked Questions

Can I pay for my domain using Indian UPI?

Yes. Many registrars operating in India (including Hostinger domain registration, Dynadot, and BigRock) accept instant UPI payments via Google Pay, PhonePe, and Paytm with zero international transaction fees.

Is a .in domain cheaper than a .com domain in India?

Yes. A .in domain typically costs between ₹499 and ₹750 per year, whereas a .com domain costs between ₹850 and ₹1,100 per year due to US dollar exchange rates. For India-focused content, .in domains rank equally well in Google.co.in search results.

Will Cloudflare Pages ever charge me for high traffic?

No. Cloudflare Pages free tier includes unmetered bandwidth. Whether your blog receives 1,000 visitors or 1,000,000 visitors in a month, Cloudflare does not charge overage fees on static assets.
